newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end up, at day's highs on cash.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end up, at day's highs on cash.

text.p: Further short covering spurred by stronger cash markets lifted CME live cattle futures to the day's highs at the close, traders said and feeder cattle ended mixed with some months rallying on a late drop in corn futures.

Live cattle closed 0.575 cent per lb higher to 0.050 lower with only December off and April up most. June ended up 0.300 at 64.875 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.500 lower to 0.175 higher with May off 0.150 at 71.000 cents.
Rising boxed beef values and expectations for higher fed cattle prices next week prompted short covering that boosted April live cattle up further late, trader said.

"There's hope that we are going to see higher cash markets next week. Packers have been a lot more aggressive coming into this week, and they have bought a lot of cattle and cleaned up the showlist," said Paul Georgy, president of Allendale Inc.

Traders cited expectations that packers will pay at least $68 per cwt for cattle in Plains direct trade next week. Some packers are short bought and also covered short positions in April as deliverable cattle supplies are tight, they said.
No delivery certificates were posted against the April contract again Friday.
April technically is also very strong, chartists said.

June hit resistance at times on speculation live prices would top in April and turn lower in the summer as more fed cattle become available. Grain futures, which posted gains part of the day, also weighed on back months, traders added.

Georgy said beef demand normally dries up in June. Retailer buying for Memorial day and Fathers day holidays is typically complete by late May and consumer interest declines as vacations cut meat consumption during the summer, he said.
RBH, R.J. O'Brien, LFG, and Cargill Investor Services notably bought April and June late. Prudential bought early while Refco and Dean Witter sold early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses spread long August 62 puts/short 66 calls and sold the 63/66 June strangle, pit sources added.

April feeders remained pressured by expected declines in the CME index the next two posting days, but prices recovered overall in feeders as corn futures turned lower late. May had been influenced all day by price swings in corn futures and rallied late to end slightly lower, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.06 at $71.19 per cwt and the outlook is for the index to lose around $0.55 the next couple of quotes.
Fall contracts showed continued support from projected heavy calf death losses in the Dakotas from recent snow storms and cold weather, they added.
Prudential Securities and R.J. O'Brien notably sold May early while LFG and STR division of Spike Trading bought. Locals bought May late, pit sources said.
